claims.claim: A platform-neutral immutable grouping contract accepts one existing MultiObservationResolutionGraph and returns immutable provisional groups without accepting source packs or invoking pairwise or multi-observation entity resolution again.

Provisional connected components are derived exclusively from existing EXACT_VARIANT_MATCH and SAME_PRODUCT_FAMILY pairwise edges in the input graph, with no independently recreated identity semantics.
The resulting groups form an exact partition of graph.observations: every SourceObservationIdentity appears exactly once, no identity is dropped or duplicated, and different groups are disjoint.

A one-member component is SINGLETON; a two-or-more-member positive component with no existing graph conflict is POSITIVE_CONNECTED; and a positive component containing one or more existing TASK-109 conflicts is CONFLICTED.
UNCERTAIN and DIFFERENT_PRODUCT pairwise decisions do not create or bridge provisional connectivity, including cases where an otherwise isolated observation remains a singleton.

CONFLICTED groups preserve the relevant ProductFamilyConsistencyConflict values already present on the TASK-109 graph and do not repair, recompute, suppress, split around, or choose a winner for contradictory evidence.

Reordering the same semantic observation set produces identical provisional group membership, canonical member ordering, group ordering, statuses, and conflict projection; positive connectivity never materializes an inferred transitive pairwise relationship.

Tests prove TASK-111 performs zero calls to the TASK-108 pairwise resolver or TASK-109 multi-observation resolver and derives no aggregate confidence, score, mergeability, or canonical identity authority.

The public grouping API performs zero filesystem mutation, persistence, network, browser, Drive, queue, LLM, scoring, ranking, approval, ingestion, catalog write, or external-service side effects and exposes no group/product/ family/variant identifier or approval field.

Focused deterministic regression tests cover a positive-connected family, singleton observations, UNCERTAIN boundaries, direct DIFFERENT_PRODUCT isolation, a conflicted positive component, multiple disjoint groups, exact partition invariants, permutation invariance, immutability, canonical output ordering, conflict preservation, and zero entity-resolution re-execution.
